status: D-023 slice 1: the frame - forged rows, sockets, supports and backing

ingots.design_purpose: Reach's base is area size on the sheet; beside a skill it speaks the 'reach' modifier instead (owner, 4 Sep 2026: Reach reads area, projectile and strike skills): a wider area, a further-flying projectile, a longer strike.

sources.design_purpose: D-021: the first time a combat skill works the world (a heavy blow drives the wedge) is a milestone - the click that the ARPG half and the sandbox half are one game pays an ingot.
The first dressed block (D-021) is a milestone: a Plate ingot, so the yard pays into the Foundry as the bench and the forge do.

design_purpose: The Foundry is the point system (docs/systems/progression-eras.md, D-019; docs/systems/foundry.md, D-023): points are INGOTS placed on a forged PLATE, and power comes from arrangement, not from the ingot's number. Every ingot is one verb (a modifier from items.json at a flat, small value that never changes). THE FRAME (D-023 slice 1, owner 4 Sep 2026): the plate is a frame of `frame` rows by columns whose rows the eras forge - `rows_by_era` lists the first and last forged row per era (the last entry serves later eras), so era one is a two-row, four-column plate, era two forges the row above it and era three the row below; nothing on the plate ever moves. `sockets` are the frame cells that take a SUBJECT (a skill tablet; later the typed currencies); an ingot never sits in a socket and a tablet never sits outside one. A WORKING is a socket, the ingots orthogonally beside it (its SUPPORTS) and the diagonal cells (its CORNERS). A support applies its modifier to the socket's skill alone at support_multiplier times its value, when the modifier can read the skill's tags; an ingot may name a `skill_modifier` it speaks beside a skill in place of its base modifier. BACKING replaces lines (owner, 4 Sep 2026): a matching ingot orthogonally touching a support, from any side but the socket's, makes that support count once more, so a duplicate ingot always has a job. Two orthogonally adjacent ingots that match a pair make that pair's mechanic for everyone. Ingots come from milestones and knowledge, never kills-per-se: sources map an event to one ingot, each once, era-gated. Re-forging (lifting an ingot) pays reforge_cost; tablets are knowledge and lift free. Era one forges twelve ingots for six free cells: the tray is the reserve and re-forging is the way between layouts. Placements a save carries in an unforged row, a tablet outside a socket or an ingot inside one are lifted free on load.
